- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.61), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates upside; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–7 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early days of a 30-day horizon; apply 0.5–1.0% upward bias for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to lag behind true price; apply 0.3–0.8% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- If recent 3–5 day price range is narrow, model often overfits to recent trend; apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias to avoid overfitting.
